name: AIJ UWE benchmark — cleaned release, Cases A-E

licence.note: The measurement data belongs to its collectors and distributors, named per case. Cite the benchmark paper and each case's requested citation.

cite.benchmark: Kikumoto, H., Okaze, T., Yoshie, R. et al. (2026). Comprehensive Experimental Database for Validating CFD Simulations in Urban Wind Environment: Benchmark Cases Curated by the Architectural Institute of Japan. Japan Architectural Review 9(1), e70083. https://doi.org/10.1002/2475-8876.70083
cite.guidelines: Tominaga, Y. et al. (2008). AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings. JWEIA 96, 1749-1761. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jweia.2008.02.058

built_by: clean/build.py (deterministic; re-run to regenerate; checks.json carries the validity checks, build.log every transform)

case_id.meaning: AIJ UWE case letter, A to M

config.meaning: configuration within the case: 'default' (A, B, D); Case C centre building '0D' | '1D' | '2D'; Case E 'bc' (before construction) | 'ac' (after construction)

instrument.meaning: 'split_fibre' = hot-wire split-fibre probe, vector components; 'thermistor' = omnidirectional scalar speed

point_id.meaning: the tunnel's own measurement point number (No.); shared across configurations and directions of a case

wind_direction_deg.meaning: the case's wind direction label. A-D: the AIJ turntable angle WD (0 = +x). E: meteorological FROM-direction, clockwise from north (N = 0, E = 90). The flow vector per direction is in directions.csv

wind_direction.meaning: compass name of the FROM-direction (Case E only; '' elsewhere)

x.meaning: case frame (SCHEMA.md): +x = streamwise at WD = 0 for A-D, +x = east for E; model-scale metres for A-D, full-scale metres for E

V.meaning: mean velocity component along +y (positive toward +y in EVERY case; Case B's published sign is flipped, see manifest transform)

uu.meaning: variance of the x-component fluctuation <u'u'> (Case A publishes rms; squared here)

k.meaning: turbulent kinetic energy as published (= (uu+vv+ww)/2 wherever all three variances exist; checked)

Vs.meaning: mean omnidirectional SCALAR wind speed from a thermistor anemometer. NOT |mean velocity vector| (Case D's split-fibre |U| column is dropped, see log)

velocity_ratio.meaning: Case E: Vs / U_ref with U_ref = the approach-flow speed at z = 15.9 m (full scale); see manifest cases.E.normalisation

campaign.meaning: 'wind_tunnel' (model scale) or 'field' (a full-scale observation: Cases F, G, M)

run.meaning: replicate label within a campaign where the dataset publishes individual runs (Case M); empty elsewhere

C.meaning: mean tracer-gas concentration as published (volume fraction x 1e6 of the released gas diluted in air)

concentration_ratio.meaning: C / c0, c0 = q / (U_ref L_ref^2) as the benchmark defines it for the case (manifest cases.<id>.normalisation)

T.meaning: mean air temperature as published (Cases J, L)

velocity_ratio_sd.meaning: standard deviation of velocity_ratio over the observations behind a field value (Case F)

k_ratio.meaning: k / U_ref^2 where the dataset publishes only normalised values (Case G; U_ref = U at the tree height)

E.title: Case E — flow within an actual urban area in Niigata
E.status_note: Case E: points and inflow are released at full precision from the official workbook and pass every check; what stays provisional is the GEOMETRY of the before-construction state (an Eddy3D reconstruction with no published source) and the open questions in QUESTIONS.md (Q3).
E.citation_requested: Tominaga, Y., Mochida, A., Yoshie, R., Kataoka, H., Nozu, T., Yoshikawa, M., Shirasawa, T. (2008). AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings. JWEIA 96, 1749-1761. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jweia.2008.02.058

frame.origin: centre of the reproduced area, ground plane ('Geometry&Points' sheet)
frame.z: +z up; every point at z = 2.0 m
frame.wind_direction_rotation: meteorological FROM-direction: N = 0 blows toward -y, E = 90 toward -x; flow_dir = (-sin WD, -cos WD). The geographic frame is kept because the district is real and both the points and the STL are published in it; the 'x along the wind' convention of A-D does not apply.
frame.length_scale: FULL-scale metres (model 1:250); the official STL is model scale and is scaled x250 here

transform_from_published.note: points unchanged (workbook values at full precision); STL x250; the 3dm-derived STLs are reoriented outward

inflow.U_ref_basis: all 2560 ratios are integer multiples of one quantum q; U_ref = 0.01 UR / q (the sheet re-normalised U/UR, itself quantised at 0.01, by UR/U_ref); log-interpolation of the profile gives the value beside it

log_law.note: does not fit — see rms_residual_rel; a tabulated inlet is the honest choice

inflow.epsilon_note: the sheet defines epsilon(z) = Pk(z) = Cmu^0.5 k(z) dU/dz with Cmu = 0.09

G.title: Case G — flow behind a tree belt (field observation)
G.citation_requested: Kurotani, Y., Kiyota, N., Kobayashi, S. (2001). Windbreak effect of Tsuijimatsu in Izumo Part. 2. Summaries of technical papers of Annual Meeting, Architectural Institute of Japan, D-2 Environmental engineering II, 745-746 (in Japanese).
G.normalisation: velocity_ratio = U/UH and k_ratio = k/UH^2, UH = the mean wind speed at the tree height z = 7 m, measured during each measurement period and interpolated with the approach flow's power law (index 0.22); no absolute speed is published. The approach-flow table carries U/Ub and k/Ub^2 instead (Ub = U at 9 m, a different day): divide by UH/Ub = 0.946 (power law) to put it on the table's normalisation.

configurations.status: unverified — field data: the angle between the wind and the belt normal is not published (QUESTIONS.md QG3)

frame.origin: the leeward face of the tree belt at ground level, on the vertical section through the belt's centre (MP_caseG.png)
frame.x: +x downwind: the belt occupies x in [-2, 0] m and the measurement lines lie behind it at x = 1.75 ... 35 m
frame.y: +y along the belt (74 m long, y in [-37, 37]); every point is on y = 0, the centre section
frame.z: +z up from the ground; the belt spans z in [1.2, 7] (1.2 m bottom gap); points at z = 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6 m
frame.wind_direction_rotation: single direction: the wind blows toward +x (perpendicular to the belt); the field angle is not published
frame.length_scale: FULL-scale metres: a field observation, no model

transform_from_published.note: U/UH and k/UH^2 from the workbook at full precision; coordinates as published; approach flow as published (U/Ub, k/Ub^2)

inflow.U_ref: Ub = mean wind speed of the approach flow at 9.0 m (not published in m/s)
inflow.lee_normalisation: RS_caseG.csv: UH = mean speed at 7 m during each measurement period (interpolated with the approach flow's power law)

H.title: Case H — flow and dispersion around a 1:1:2 building (floor point source)
H.citation_requested: Yoshie, R. (2016). Wind Tunnel Experiment and Large Eddy Simulation of Pollutant/Thermal Dispersion in Non-isothermal Turbulent Boundary Layer. Adv Environ Wind Eng, 167-196. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-4-431-55912-2_9
H.normalisation: velocity by U_H = 3.226 m/s (the approach flow at z = H = 0.2 m; 3.23 in the readme and the paper), k by U_H^2; concentration_ratio = C / c0 with c0 = cgas q / (U_H H^2) = 1e6 ppm x 5.83e-6 m3/s / (3.226 m/s x 0.2^2 m2) = 45.18 ppm (the workbook; the paper rounds it to 45.2). The workbook's reference speed U0 = 5.279 m/s is the free stream, not U_H.

frame.origin: the centre of the building's leeward face on the ground plane (MP-y_caseH.png, MP-z_caseH.png)
frame.x: +x streamwise (the wind blows toward +x): the building occupies x in [-0.1, 0]; points at x = -0.2 .. 0.4 m
frame.y: +y lateral; the building spans y in [-0.05, 0.05]; the z = 0.0625H plane covers y in [-0.2, 0.2], the others y in [0, 0.2] and the y = 0 line
frame.z: +z up; roof at z = 0.2 m; points at z = 0.01 .. 0.3 m
frame.source: the 4 mm floor hole at (0.05, 0, 0), i.e. 0.25 H behind the leeward face
frame.length_scale: model metres (the source states no model:full scale ratio; Eddy3D solves it at 1:100)

transform_from_published.lateral_sign: -1 for point numbers 1-220 (the vertical-plane sheet), +1 elsewhere
transform_from_published.note: U, V, W, rms and k = the workbook's ratios x uH (uH^2 for k), V of point numbers 1-220 multiplied by -1; variances = (rms x uH)^2; concentration as published; one row per instrument; the x = 400 mm label of 18 concentration-only rows is read as 380 mm

inflow.method: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 2H on the workbook's 17-point inflow profile
inflow.note: the approach-flow table's uu, vv, ww are (rms x uH)^2; the profile's uw and uv are in the workbook and the CSV but have no column in the approach-flow table

I.title: Case I — flow and dispersion around a cube (roof point source)
data_collectors: Hiroaki Kondo (National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology)
Katsuhiko Mutou (National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology)
Akihiro Hori (National Institute for Environmental Studies)
I.citation_requested: Japan Society for Atmospheric Environment (2013). Guidelines for Atmospheric Environment Assessment Methods Using CFD Models (DiMCFD). Japan Society for Atmospheric Environment (in Japanese).
I.normalisation: velocity by U_H = 1.7 m/s (the readme; the approach flow at z = H = 0.1 m is 1.697 m/s), concentration_ratio = C / c0 with c0 = 39.2235 ppm (the workbook; the paper rounds it to 39.2) = q / (U_H H^2) for q = the ETHANE flow, 10 % of the 400 cc/min released (6.67e-7 m3/s), not the 6.67e-6 m3/s the paper quotes for the mixture.

frame.origin: the centre of the cube on the ground plane (MP-y-c_caseI.png, MP-z-c_caseI.png)
frame.x: +x streamwise (the wind blows toward +x): the cube occupies x in [-0.05, 0.05]; wind points x = -0.15 .. 0.25, concentration points x = 0.065 .. 2.7
frame.y: +y lateral; the cube spans y in [-0.05, 0.05]; wind points on y = 0 and on the plane z = 0.05 at |y| <= 0.15, concentration points on y = 0 and on the ground at |y| <= 0.44
frame.z: +z up; roof at z = 0.1 m; the source (6 mm outlet) at (0, 0, 0.1)
frame.source: ethane, 10 % in the mixture, 400 cc/min through a 6 mm circular outlet at the roof centre (M = 0.14)
frame.length_scale: model metres (the source states no model:full scale ratio; Eddy3D solves it at 1:60)

transform_from_published.note: values from the workbook; one row per instrument, wind rows 1-91 and concentration rows 92-630; V on the y = 0 plane set to NaN; coordinates as published

inflow.U_ref_basis: the measured U at z = H; the 'Velocity measurement' sheet and every ratio of the points use 1.7
inflow.method: least squares, kappa = 0.41, z = 0.02 .. 0.4 m on the workbook's 12-point profile
inflow.tunnel: 20 m long, 3.0 x 2.0 m cross-section (paper section 3.9)
inflow.note: the approach-flow table's uu, vv, ww are empty: only k is published; set wind speed 3.2 (the workbook's first cell, Japanese label) is the tunnel setting
